title: Privacy, Security & Data Boundaries
summary: Learn why workplace information must be handled according to privacy, security, authorization, and data-use boundaries—especially when using digital and AI tools.
objectives: Recognize common categories of sensitive workplace information.
Explain why approved tools and authorization matter when sharing or entering data.
Identify when uncertain data handling should be stopped and clarified.

vocab.def: Information that may require additional protection because misuse or exposure could cause harm.
Information that an organization restricts from unauthorized access or disclosure.
Giving a person or system only the access needed for an approved responsibility.
A rule or restriction governing where information may be stored, shared, processed, or used.

sections.heading: Not all workplace information should be treated the same
sections.body: Workplaces may handle personal information, customer records, financial information, health information, credentials, internal plans, trade information, or other restricted material.

sections.heading: Protect information before using a tool
sections.body: Before uploading, copying, pasting, sharing, or entering workplace information into a digital or AI tool, confirm that the tool and the use are allowed.

sections.heading: Use only the access you need
sections.body: Least-privilege thinking reduces unnecessary exposure. Having broader technical access does not mean every file, field, account, or record should be viewed or used.

sections.heading: Stop when the boundary is unclear
sections.body: If you are unsure whether information is private, confidential, restricted, or allowed in a particular tool, pause and ask the appropriate person rather than guessing.

practice.prompt: You want to paste customer information into an AI assistant to create a summary, but you do not know whether the tool is approved. What should you do?
practice.answer: Do not enter the information until the tool, data use, and authorization are confirmed.

practice.prompt: You discover you can access a confidential folder that is unrelated to your work. What is the responsible response?
practice.answer: Do not use the information simply because access is technically possible; follow the appropriate process if the access appears incorrect.

quiz.question: What should happen before sensitive workplace information is entered into an AI tool?
options: Confirm that the tool and use are approved for that information
Remove the file name and upload it anyway
Assume any workplace tool is safe
quiz.answer: Confirm that the tool and use are approved for that information

lab.objective: Classify simulated information-handling scenarios as approved, needs clarification, restricted, or inappropriate without using any real sensitive information.

reflectionPrompt: Why is protecting information part of professional responsibility even when no one explicitly reminds you?
